clue.text: If wet, he heads off for holiday

indicators.note: the heads of the three words If, wet and he are each cut off, leaving what follows them

explanation.surface: If it rains, a holidaymaker decides to set off for a break elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' removes the first letter of each of If, wet and he, leaving F, ET and E to run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festival or celebration, and a holiday in the old sense of a feast day.

clue.text: Student probing eggs' substance

indicators.note: a student probing the eggs is placed inside them, the probe going in among them

parts.note: an egg is shaped like the letter O, so several eggs give a row of Os
L is the learner plate, a student driver's mark
the gist of something is its essence or substance

explanation.surface: A researcher pokes at eggs to find out what they are made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a specialist in eggs is a student probing them.
explanation.definitionFit: An oologist is a scientist who studies birds' eggs, so a student probing eggs fits exactly.

clue.text: Keeps interrupting woman from the floor to paraphrase

indicators.note: one word interrupting another is put into the middle of it
in a down clue, reading up from the floor means the word woman's letters run upwards, backwards

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
keeps means has, holds on to

explanation.surface: Someone keeps cutting into a woman's speech from the floor of a meeting to restate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the floor' turns HER upwards to REH; 'interrupting' puts HAS into it, giving RE-HAS-H.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehash material is to restate it in other words with little change, which is to paraphrase it.

clue.text: Row about non-U voice is source of nervous laughter

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes round it on both sides

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: non-U, punning on the upper-class usage label, says the letter U is dropped from the word for voice

parts.note: to voice something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A row about an unrefined manner of speaking causes uneasy giggles.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is a British label, from the 1950s, for speech or manners thought not upper-class; here it simply drops a U.
explanation.definitionFit: One who titters giggles nervously, so a titterer produces nervous laughter.

clue.text: Oscar wearing Chanel's new wrap

indicators.note: Oscar wearing the other pieces sits inside them, clothed by them

parts.note: Coco was the first name of the fashion designer Chanel
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner is dressed in a new Chanel wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts O between COCO and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is a silky case an insect spins round itself, so it is a wrap or covering.

clue.text: Siemens once evacuated Munich, returning thereafter

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outer letters of Munich remain
returning means the word for thereafter is read backwards

parts.note: so means then, thereafter, as in 'and so it went'

explanation.surface: The Siemens company once left Munich and later went back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Siemens the German firm; here it is the SI unit of conductance.
explanation.definitionFit: The mho was the former name for the unit of electrical conductance now called the siemens.

clue.text: Kisses Nurse Roe roughly, escapes without clothes and runs off

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so the kisses cradle the other letters

parts.note: X is the sign for a kiss at the end of a letter, so two kisses give two Xs

indicators.note: roughly signals a rough rearrangement of the word Roe
without here means taken away from, so the clothing word is removed from escapes

parts.note: capes are garments, clothes

explanation.surface: A man kisses a nurse called Roe clumsily, escapes naked and runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' reads as a person, but it is the container signal, holding the rearranged Roe.
explanation.definitionFit: To xerox is to photocopy, and running off copies is an idiom for printing them.

clue.text: Life is short: love your man

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the word for life loses its last letter

parts.note: a life sentence is time served in prison
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark that life is brief, so love your partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the E from TIME to give TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is a man's first name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: Cherokee boxing champion

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the word Cherokee holds the answer inside itself

explanation.surface: A Native American title-holder in the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a champion, someone admired for courage or achievement.

clue.text: Panda is to evolve in Darwinian processes

indicators.note: to evolve is to change form, so the letters of the phrase change into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that pandas must adapt as Darwin's theory demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptations, also spelt adaptions, are the changes by which species fit their surroundings in Darwin's theory of evolution.

clue.text: Cornered gnu dealt a blow

indicators.note: a blow knocks things about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A wildebeest trapped in a corner is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt a blow' looks like one phrase, but dealt and a are part of the letters to rearrange, and blow alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Angulated means having angles or corners, so it means cornered in its literal sense.

clue.text: Arachne's brains regularly obliterated by hard whiskey

parts.note: Arachne is the setter, who speaks of herself as I

indicators.note: every other letter of brains is wiped out at regular intervals, leaving the rest

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The setter says too much hard liquor has wiped out her brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly obliterated' strikes out B, A and N from brains, leaving RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is short for Irish whiskey, the spirit made in Ireland and spelt with an e.

clue.text: Hurt, Jack lost temper

indicators.note: lost means the jack letter has gone missing from the word for hurt

parts.note: to injure is to hurt
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Jack was hurt and lost his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to harden or toughen someone by exposure, as metal is tempered.

clue.text: Brave child, for example, rebelling against head of orphanage

indicators.note: rebelling means turning against, so the words for child and for example are turned backwards

parts.note: a minor is a child in law

indicators.note: the head of orphanage is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bold youngster stands up against the person running the children's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebelling' turns MINOREG into GERONIM; then O from orphanage. 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was an Apache leader, and a Native American warrior is called a brave.

clue.text: Concepts spread from individual to individual on Sunday

parts.note: me is the individual speaking, one person
a second me, the next individual

explanation.surface: Ideas pass from one person to the next at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Memes are ideas or behaviours passed from person to person, so they are concepts that spread.

clue.text: New wine, which shouldn't be neglected

definitions.meaning: freshly pressed grape juice before fermentation is finished is a winemaker's term for young wine
something essential that ought not to be missed is called a necessity

explanation.surface: A young vintage that nobody should overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Must is unfermented grape juice, and a must is something essential, two separate senses of the word.

clue.text: Coe, perhaps, scratching front of Beamer

indicators.note: scratching the front of the word means its first letter is struck out

parts.note: someone who beams is smiling, a smiler

explanation.surface: Sebastian Coe crashes a BMW, scraping its bonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beamer' is British slang for a BMW car, which the surface wants; here it is one who beams, a SMILER, losing S. Sebastian Coe was a British middle-distance runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebastian Coe was a champion runner over the mile, and 'perhaps' marks him as an example.

clue.text: Memorial United Nations put up in less than no time

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters go inside the word for a very short time

parts.note: a moment is an instant, the briefest of times

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are raised, read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: The United Nations erected a war memorial in record speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' suits a down clue, where the letters climb from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is a statue or structure built to commemorate a person or event, so it is a memorial.

clue.text: Rocky grey miles where fossils are found

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A stony grey coastline stretching for miles where ancient remains lie.
explanation.walkthrough: LYME REGIS is a seaside town in Dorset, England, on the Jurassic Coast, famous for fossil hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyme Regis is the Dorset resort whose cliffs and beaches are famous for fossils, so it is a place they are found.

clue.text: Lass is receiving protection to stop being criminal

indicators.note: receiving means one piece takes in the other, which goes inside it

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind, protection
a gal is a girl, a lass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl takes shelter to stop being a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' makes LEE take in GAL and IS. The definition means 'cause to stop being criminal'.
explanation.definitionFit: To legalise an act is to make it lawful, so it stops being a crime.

clue.text: Spooner's ringing repartee is tightly constructed

indicators.note: Spooner's marks a swapping of initial sounds between two words, after Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a knell is the ringing of a bell
wit is clever repartee

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner's ringing banter is neatly put together.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoonerisms are named after the Reverend William Spooner, famed for swapping the opening sounds of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-knit describes something firmly joined or compactly built, so tightly constructed.

clue.text: Antics of Cyril Knowles ultimately inspire words of popular song

indicators.note: antics are capers, so the letters of the name caper into a new order
ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of Knowles

explanation.surface: Cyril Knowles's capers ended up inspiring a pop song.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyril Knowles was a Tottenham Hotspur footballer about whom the pop song 'Nice One Cyril' was written.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrics are the words of a song, especially a popular one.

clue.text: See 17
Consider knockers essentially funny

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are put in an odd new order
essentially means at its core, so the word knockers loses its ends and keeps the middle

explanation.surface: A risqué remark that knockers are basically a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' leaves NOCKER from knockers; 'funny' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to think or judge, to consider something so.

clue.text: Quiet, dedicated leader in America trained as emergency worker

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: trained means schooled into shape, so the letters are reshaped
the leader of dedicated is its first letter

explanation.surface: A quiet, committed American is trained to work in emergencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader in America' looks like one phrase meaning A, but leader belongs with dedicated and in is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a trained ambulance worker giving first aid at emergencies.

clue.text: Michael Portillo's entertaining ex post facto excuse

indicators.note: ex post facto means after the event, looking back, so the letters are read backwards
entertaining means holding as a guest, so the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: Michael Portillo offers an excuse after the fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' finds AELP across michAEL Portillo; 'ex post facto' turns it round. Michael Portillo is a former British Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an excuse or appeal offered in one's defence.

clue.text: Live wire shot chief usher

definitions.meaning: to live a certain life is to conduct it in a given way, as in a quiet existence
the soft metal that bullets and shot are made from
to guide or conduct someone ahead

explanation.surface: An energetic man who fired a gun is the head steward.
explanation.walkthrough: Five separate definitions: lead a life, an electric lead, lead shot, the lead role, and to lead someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead has many senses: to live a life, an electrical flex, the metal of shot, main, and to guide.

clue.text: Final word of boundless sorrow

indicators.note: boundless means without its bounds, so the word for sorrow loses both end letters

parts.note: a lament is an expression of sorrow

explanation.surface: The last thing said in limitless grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the end of a prayer or hymn, so it is the closing word.

clue.text: Decline to express different opinion on radio

indicators.note: on radio means as heard broadcast, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

parts.note: dissent is disagreement, a differing opinion

explanation.surface: Refusing to air a dissenting view on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like 'refuse', but it is a noun: a downward slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or a fall, so a decline.

clue.text: What people said that's welcomed by senior Indianan

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for what people is heard, not spelt

parts.note: who asks what people, which persons

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, put inside the other piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something people said that was well received by an elderly man from Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoosier is said to come from the frontier greeting 'Who's here?', which the clue plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoosier is the nickname for a native or resident of the US state of Indiana.
